title: Where is the middle of a ring of birds?

data.source: Frechet (1948) and Kuramoto (1975) as definitions; Mardia (1972). Computed on the example of Phoenix_Egg/CORE/MATHEMATICS.md section V and on 4500 random draws, seeded.

prediction: R5's Frechet mean on a circle is not the Kuramoto phase: on the contents (0, 0, pi) the Frechet mean has two answers for every q while the Kuramoto phase has one, except at the golden q where the order parameter r is exactly 0; the two means agree only when the contents are bunched.
baseline: The Frechet mean (1948) and the Kuramoto order parameter (1975), each as defined.
why: The seed on a circle is not the Kuramoto phase: on R5's own example the two differed by 1.35 radians at q = 0.5, and on widely spread contents they differed in most draws. They agreed to a few thousandths of a radian when contents were bunched. One thing the comparison explains: the golden q in R5's example is exactly where the Kuramoto order parameter vanishes, which is what "equal total weight" picks out; the Frechet tie is there for every q, as Phoenix's anomaly note already records. Neither fact makes the golden ratio a prediction, and Phoenix says so.
